title: sdks: unify auth/retries/streaming ergonomics across python/typescript/go and bump versions to v1.61.0
author: Aisha Khan
description: Unify authentication surfaces, retry behavior, and streaming ergonomics across the Python, TypeScript, and Go SDKs and bump package versions to v1.61.0. Motivation: several downstream teams reported inconsistencies in token refresh behavior, streaming client APIs, and subtle parity gaps between SDKs leading to maintenance burden and confusion in examples. This PR: 1) standardizes auth handling so all SDKs expose a single TokenProvider interface/abstraction with optional automatic refresh and pluggable KMS/HSM hooks; 2) implements a shared retry policy (exponential backoff with jitter, transparent idempotency key propagation for non-streaming requests, and clear opt-out) and surfaces it consistently in init/config; 3) brings streaming parity: server->client event framing helpers, backpressure-friendly async iterators (python/ts) and channel-based reader (go), unified close/error propagation semantics; 4) ergonomics: sync/async parity in Python, promise-friendly helpers in TS, and clearer docs and type defs; 5) updates changelogs and bumps package versions to v1.61.0 for python/typescript/go. Migration notes included in changelogs: minor default retry policy change (safer defaults) but fully configurable, token provider API stable for common use cases; guidance provided for advanced custom providers. This is primarily non-breaking for most users but please review migration notes before cutting releases.
commits: initial: add TokenProvider abstraction and adapters for python/ts/go
refactor: extract common retry policy and test harness
feat(streaming): unify event framing and async iterators/readers
docs: changelog and migration notes for v1.61.0
fix(tests): address race in python token refresh test
chore: bump package versions to v1.61.0
review_comments: Martin: Please clarify race conditions for token refresh when multiple requests trigger refresh simultaneously. Can we add a single-flight guard?
Aisha: Added a single-flight guard in python and go; TS uses a promise dedupe. See commits 3-4.
Elena: Streaming parser looks good, but the TS types for partial events are loose. Can we tighten the definitions so generated output types are preserved?
Aisha: tightened TS event types and added unit tests to ensure output shape stability.
Samir: We should avoid enabling the new retry policy by default for customers using legacy idempotency keys until a migration window passes.
Aisha: Agree. Default is safer exponential-with-jitter; added explicit opt-out and changelog guidance. Will notify customers via release notes.
Ravi: CI flaked on go integration once - re-ran and all green. Add an integration test that simulates streaming disconnects.
Aisha: Added integration test that asserts graceful reconnect/close behavior. CI green now.
Martin: Approve after CI green and changelog updates.
Samir: Approve with release note callout.
release_notes: Auth: Introduce TokenProvider abstraction and optional automatic refresh with KMS/HSM hooks
Retries: Default safe exponential backoff with jitter; idempotency propagation for non-streaming requests; configurable and opt-out
Streaming: unified event framing, backpressure-friendly iterators/readers, consistent close/error semantics
Docs: migration guide included; default retry change - read migration note before upgrade
